name_reason: Follows fd2_<domain>_<descriptor>; '24x24' is the meaningful sprite dimension (domain knowledge, not address residue) and 'with_tint_offset' accurately describes the palette-band tint behaviour, consistent with the fd2_tile_blit_24x24_* family (passthrough/remap/with_remap_table/solid_color/dimmed_grayscale/with_dialog_bg_fill). No Ghidra address residue.
purpose: Hand-written RLE blit of a 24x24 sprite into dst_buf, recolouring every painted pixel into an 8-colour palette band as ((src_pixel + team_offset) & 7) + color_base.
logic_summary: Outer loop runs 24 rows; per row x_remain starts at 0x18 and is decremented per RLE command until 0, then dst advances by (stride - 0x18) to the next row. Each command byte's top 2 bits select the mode and low 6 bits + 1 give the run length: 00=RUN (one tinted source byte painted contiguously), 01=STRIDE-2 RUN (one tinted source byte painted at every other dst byte, x -= 2*count), 10=LITERAL (count tinted source bytes copied), 11=SKIP (advance dst, no source consumed). The tint transform is purely arithmetic: (uint8)(((uint8)(src_byte + team_offset)) & 7) + color_base, keeping the pixel within an 8-colour band starting at color_base, shifted within the octet by team_offset, with no remap LUT. Leaf function: no __CHK stack probe, no CALLs.
signature: void fd2_tile_blit_24x24_with_tint_offset(uint32 rle_stream, uint32 dst_buf, uint32 stride, uint32 color_base, uint32 team_offset)

params.name: rle_stream
params.semantics: Source RLE-encoded 24x24 sprite stream (linear address; Ghidra types it byte *).
params.reason: Accurately names the source RLE stream; no address residue.

params.name: dst_buf
params.semantics: Destination base linear address that receives the 24x24 blit.
params.reason: Accurately names the destination buffer; no address residue.

params.name: stride
params.semantics: Destination row stride in bytes (0x1C8 from the sole caller); row reset advances dst by (stride - 0x18).
params.reason: Accurate; matches the sibling blitters' stride param.

params.name: color_base
params.semantics: Palette band anchor / base index (low byte used); added after the &7 mask. The sole caller passes the per-spell tint mask byte (mask_tbl[spell_id]) here.
params.reason: Accurately describes the band anchor used as the additive base; no address residue.

params.name: team_offset
params.semantics: Octet-rotation add value applied to each source pixel before the &7 mask (low byte used). The sole caller (fd2_animate_spell_overlay_blink) passes 7 - (frame % 8), i.e. a fade step sweeping 7..0 across the 10-frame animation -- NOT a per-team id.
params.reason: Name 'team_offset' is a misnomer: the function is named *_with_tint_offset and the sole caller passes a fade step (7..0), never a team id. 'tint_offset' matches the function name and the actual octet-rotation/tint semantics. No address residue; rename is purely semantic-accuracy. (Apply in Stage 2 across protos.h + body + plate.)

returns.semantics: No return value; effect is the in-place tinted blit into dst_buf.

comment_original_issue: Src comment described team_offset as giving a 'per-team / per-fade colour variation', but no per-team usage exists -- the sole caller only ever passes a fade step (7..0). Refined the semantic sentence and the param-list line to state the octet-rotation/fade meaning precisely, and noted that color_base receives the per-spell tint mask byte from the caller.
notes: Body verified against Ghidra decompile and the sole caller (fd2_animate_spell_overlay_blink @ 0x1CD17 in src/anim/anicombt.c). Src signature uses uint32 linear-address params (Layer-2 convention) vs Ghidra's byte*/char*; types left untouched per refine rules. No logic touched. The function is one of seven sibling fd2_tile_blit_24x24_* variants sharing the same RLE syntax; this one applies the additive 8-colour band tint.
